# Disjoint VDOM batch roots escape in-flight protection

## Context

While restoring Demo B's full tour on #19461, a native headless journey at Engine `6e19f6031b` produced two insertNode births for one new tab-header id in successive mixed-root and toolbar flights. Worker and VDOM membership are unique; DOM membership remains duplicated through a five-second consistency check.

A read-only pre-send scope probe now records a collected merged host with childUpdateDepth=-1 and distance=1, while only its initiating workspace is registered at depth1. The host's in-flight entry is absent and isVdomUpdating is false. Main's corresponding response contains both workspace and host vnode roots.

## The Problem

`VdomLifecycle#executeVdomUpdate` registers only its initiating component. Payload collection can emit additional same-window, disjoint component roots. Those roots have real in-flight subtrees but do not participate in the existing updating flag/registry guard, allowing a descendant to start a conflicting flight against an older baseline.

Design authority: `VDomUpdate#registerInFlightUpdate` marks an update sent to the worker; `VdomLifecycle#isParentUpdating` uses that component's flag and captured depth to defer overlapping descendants. A collected disjoint root must carry that same protection.

The prior `#17991` repair coheres an existing owner's escalated depth. Its own final body retracts a duplicate-render consequence and distinguishes `#17999`'s canonical-reference cure. Neither establishes protection for an additional emitted root; the present runtime record is the new discriminator.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs` owns collection, collision filtering, response adoption and failure release.
- `src/manager/VDomUpdate.mjs` already owns in-flight depth, promises and post-update queues.
- `test/playwright/unit/vdom/VdomLifecycle.spec.mjs` is the existing state/flight owner.
- SharedWorker payload collection excludes another window; that boundary must remain intact.

## The Fix

Bring every emitted disjoint component root into the existing in-flight lifecycle using its captured depth. Adopt its response before releasing blocked descendants. A rejected batch must release each tracked root, its parked promises and post-update work; do not strand a borrowed flag or overwrite a later cycle.

Use the existing registry/guard primitives. Do not change the Main insertNode apply layer or deduplicate DOM after publication. A deterministic behavioral unit and the live duplicate control decide whether the proposed protection resolves the observed rendering consequence.

## Contract Ledger

| Surface | Authority | Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Disjoint batch root guard | Existing updating flag + in-flight depth contract | Every emitted same-window root is protected at its captured depth | Existing post-update deferral | Owning JSDoc | Deferred descendant write with held batch |
| Batch completion/failure | Existing VDOM flight outcome contract | Adopt first; release all tracked scopes/promises on success or rejection | Existing retry/rejection contract | Owning JSDoc | Success, rejection and late-promise controls |

Decision Record impact: none — restoration of existing VDOM flight ownership. No new wire/config surface.
Structure map: N/A — existing Body mixin/manager and source-mirror unit spec; no new module.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A deterministic mixed-root batch reproduces an unprotected deep root on the old source.
- [ ] Each emitted same-window root has its captured depth and updating protection; a descendant's conflicting write waits until response adoption.
- [ ] Success and rejection release the correct scopes, callbacks and post-update work; late promises retain their next-cycle semantics.
- [ ] Other-window roots remain excluded and are not incorrectly marked as part of the batch.
- [ ] The native duplicate control and a subsequent toolbar write remain coherent with the prerequisite witness candidate; focused receipts name both source layers.
- [ ] Owning unit checks pass and the result is linked to #17844/#19461; no full-battery or headed acceptance claim.

## Out of Scope

Main DOM deduplication, catalog/schema changes, Demo B witness/cue repairs, and new rendering services.

## Avoided Traps

No consumer sleep or redundant-commit suppression as the engine cure; that candidate was experimentally falsified. No depth freezing, because it can exclude legitimate subtree work. No inference that the older registry-value cure fixed a duplicate it did not reproduce.
